subject: Residuals Calculations and Diagnostics in INLA

messages.author: 5c834f66d44ea056
messages.subject: Residuals Calculations and Diagnostics in INLA
parts:
Hello INLA experts,

I am  new to INLA package and using in which my dependent variable is observed cases of a disease like this
formula <- Y ~
  f(id, model = "besag", graph = g, scale.model = TRUE) +
  f(id1, model = "iid")

where Y is the observed cases

res <- inla(formula,
  family = "poisson", data = map@data,
  E = Expected, control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE)
)

Wanted to ask if the output does produce the residuals or do I
have to calculate it after producing the output.
If I have to calculate what will be the formula for it?

Thanks!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Residuals Calculations and Diagnostics in INLA
parts:
you can always compare data wrt the fitted values, like the PIT values,
or do something yourself. in the Bayesian context, there is no such
thing as a 'residual', its more a distribution of residuals.
